questions.q: Which is the oldest National Park in India, originally established in 1936 as Hailey National Park?
questions.explanation: Jim Corbett National Park in Nainital/Pauri Garhwal district of Uttarakhand was established in 1936 as Hailey National Park. It was India's first national park and the inaugural site of Project Tiger in 1973.

questions.q: Which UNESCO World Heritage National Park in Assam holds the world's largest population of the Great Indian One-Horned Rhinoceros?
questions.explanation: Kaziranga National Park in Assam, located on the fertile floodplains of the Brahmaputra River, hosts roughly two-thirds of the world's Great Indian One-Horned Rhinoceros population.

questions.q: Keibul Lamjao National Park, famous as the world's only floating national park and home to the endangered Sangai (dancing deer), is situated on which water body?
questions.explanation: Keibul Lamjao National Park is situated on Loktak Lake in Bishnupur district, Manipur. It is characterized by floating decomposed plant matter known locally as phumdis.

questions.q: Which is the largest National Park in India by geographical area, globally renowned as a prime habitat for the elusive Snow Leopard?
questions.explanation: Hemis National Park in eastern Ladakh spans approximately 4,400 sq km, making it India's largest national park. It sits in the high-altitude Trans-Himalayas and is famous for high snow leopard density.

questions.q: Gir National Park in Gujarat is the only natural wild sanctuary in the world for which apex predator?
questions.explanation: Gir National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary in Saurashtra, Gujarat, is the sole remaining natural wild habitat of the Asiatic Lion (Panthera leo persica).

questions.q: Sundarbans National Park in West Bengal is formed by the confluence of which major river delta systems?
questions.explanation: Sundarbans is the world's largest mangrove delta formed by the sediment of the Ganga, Brahmaputra, and Meghna rivers, famous for tidal Royal Bengal Tigers and estuarine saltwater crocodiles.

questions.q: Which national park in Madhya Pradesh is famous for saving the hard-ground swamp deer (Barasingha) and introducing "Bhoorsingh the Barasingha" as its official mascot?
questions.explanation: Kanha National Park saved the hard-ground swamp deer (Rucervus duvaucelii branderi) from near extinction and became the first tiger reserve in India to introduce an official mascot, Bhoorsingh.

questions.q: Silent Valley National Park in the Nilgiri Hills of Kerala is nourished by which river and famous for which endangered primate?
questions.explanation: Silent Valley National Park in Palakkad district, Kerala, is drained by the pristine Kunthipuzha River and protects the largest viable wild population of the endangered Lion-tailed Macaque.

questions.q: Which national park in Sikkim was inscribed in 2016 as India's first and only UNESCO "Mixed" World Heritage Site (for both natural and cultural significance)?
questions.explanation: Khangchendzonga National Park covers the third highest peak on Earth (Mt. Kanchenjunga) and sacred Buddhist Beyul cultural sites, making it India's unique UNESCO Mixed World Heritage Site.

questions.q: Which is the smallest National Park in India by land area, measuring approximately 0.03 square kilometers (3 hectares)?
options: South Button Island National Park (Andaman & Nicobar Islands)
questions.explanation: South Button Island National Park in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands is India's smallest national park with an area of about 0.03 sq km, famed for pristine shallow-water coral reefs.

questions.q: Dachigam National Park near Srinagar in Jammu & Kashmir is the last surviving natural stronghold for which critically endangered deer species?
questions.explanation: Dachigam National Park protects the critically endangered Hangul or Kashmir Stag (Cervus hanglu hanglu), the only surviving species of red deer in India, along the Dagwan River.

questions.q: Which high-altitude national park in Jammu and Kashmir is situated in the Chenab River basin, bounded by the Rinnay and Kibar rivers?
questions.explanation: Kishtwar National Park in Kishtwar district of Jammu & Kashmir lies in the Central Himalayan alpine zone between the Rinnay and Kibar rivers, famous for the Himalayan Snowcock and Brown Bear.

questions.q: Kazinag National Park along the Line of Control in Baramulla district of Jammu & Kashmir was specifically established to conserve which rare wild goat with spiral corkscrew horns?
questions.explanation: Kazinag National Park on the north bank of the Jhelum River was notified in 2007 to protect the endangered Markhor, the largest wild goat in the world famous for its magnificent flared spiral horns.

questions.q: Which river forms the northern boundary of the high-altitude Hemis National Park in Ladakh, India's largest national park?
questions.explanation: Hemis National Park is bounded on the north by the Indus River and spans 4,400 sq km of Trans-Himalayan high plateau, hosting Hemis Gompa and the world's highest density of Snow Leopards.

questions.q: Great Himalayan National Park (GHNP), inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2014 for its Outstanding Universal Value in biodiversity, is located in which district of Himachal Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Great Himalayan National Park is located in Kullu district of Himachal Pradesh, protecting the catchments of the Tirthan, Sainj, Jiwa Nal, and Parvati rivers.

questions.q: Pin Valley National Park in Himachal Pradesh preserves the unique high-altitude cold desert flora and fauna of which valley?
questions.explanation: Pin Valley National Park lies entirely within the Spiti subdivision of Lahaul & Spiti district in the Trans-Himalayan Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve, home to the Siberian Ibex and Snow Leopard.

questions.q: Which rapid alpine stream, an upstream tributary of the Bhyundar Ganga, drains the enchanting UNESCO World Heritage meadows of Valley of Flowers National Park in Uttarakhand?
questions.explanation: Valley of Flowers National Park in Chamoli district is drained by the Pushpawati River, discovered by British mountaineer Frank S. Smythe in 1931 and famed for over 500 species of alpine flora.

questions.q: Nanda Devi National Park surrounds India's second highest mountain peak (7,816 m). Through which formidable glacial gorge does its only drainage escape?
questions.explanation: The Nanda Devi Sanctuary is enclosed by a ring of 6,000-meter peaks, with its glacial waters draining solely through the impassable Rishi Ganga Gorge into the Dhauli Ganga.

questions.q: Rajaji National Park in the Shivalik foothills of Uttarakhand was created in 1983 by amalgamating Chilla, Motichur, and which other historic sanctuary?
questions.explanation: Rajaji National Park was formed by merging Rajaji Sanctuary, Motichur Sanctuary, and Chilla Sanctuary, named after freedom fighter C. Rajagopalachari (Rajaji). It is a vital Asian Elephant habitat.

questions.q: Which historic 10th-century UNESCO World Heritage hill fort overlooks the lakes and tiger territory of Ranthambore National Park in Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: Ranthambore Fort sits atop a 700-foot hill inside Ranthambore National Park in Sawai Madhopur, bounded by the Banas and Chambal rivers and famous for diurnal tiger viewing.

questions.q: Desert National Park in Jaisalmer and Barmer districts of Rajasthan is the most crucial sanctuary for which critically endangered avian species, known locally as Godawan?
questions.explanation: Desert National Park covers ~3,162 sq km of Thar sand dunes and scrubland, providing the last major breeding habitat for the Great Indian Bustard (Rajasthan's state bird).

questions.q: Which was India's first notified Marine National Park, established in 1982 to protect coral reefs, mangroves, and 42 islands in Gujarat?
options: Marine National Park, Gulf of Kutch
Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park
questions.explanation: Marine National Park in the Gulf of Kutch (Jamnagar district, Gujarat) was declared in 1982 as India's first marine national park, protecting 162 sq km of coral reefs and mangrove islands like Pirotan.

questions.q: Kanha National Park in Madhya Pradesh achieved international acclaim for saving which subspecies of deer from the brink of extinction, introducing "Bhoorsingh the Barasingha" as its official mascot?
questions.explanation: Kanha National Park saved the central Indian Hardground Barasingha (Rucervus duvaucelii branderi) from fewer than 66 individuals in 1970 to over 800 today, becoming the first reserve in India to introduce an official mascot.

questions.q: Which national park in Umaria district of Madhya Pradesh is celebrated for the highest recorded density of Bengal Tigers in India and the historic origin of the white tiger Mohan?
questions.explanation: Bandhavgarh National Park has the highest tiger density in India, centered around ancient Bandhavgarh hill and the 2000-year-old fort gifted by Lord Rama to brother Lakshmana.

questions.q: Which pristine river flows through the heart of Panna National Park in Madhya Pradesh, creating spectacular gorges and waterfalls like Pandav Falls?
questions.explanation: The Ken River flows northwards through Panna National Park, supporting gharials, muggers, and vulture nesting cliffs, and is the focal point of the Ken-Betwa river linking project.

questions.q: Satpura National Park forms the core wilderness of which UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, featuring Mount Dhoopgarh, the highest point in Madhya Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Satpura National Park in Narmadapuram is part of the Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve. Dhoopgarh peak (1,350 m) provides dramatic sandstone ravines and Malabar Giant Squirrel habitat.

questions.q: Under Project Cheetah, Southeast African cheetahs were reintroduced to which National Park in the Sheopur district of Madhya Pradesh in September 2022?
questions.explanation: Kuno National Park along the Kuno River was chosen for the reintroduction of cheetahs 70 years after their extinction in India due to its expansive open grasslands and abundant prey base.

questions.q: Notified in 1955 in Chandrapur district, which is Maharashtra's oldest and largest National Park, famously referred to as "The Jewel of Vidarbha"?
questions.explanation: Tadoba National Park (combined with Andhari Wildlife Sanctuary to form Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve) is the oldest national park in Maharashtra, taking its name from the local deity Taru.

questions.q: Which national park, situated within Mumbai's suburban metropolis, houses the ancient 1st-century BCE rock-cut Kanheri Buddhist Caves?
questions.explanation: Sanjay Gandhi National Park in Borivali, Mumbai, is one of the few national parks situated within a mega-city metropolis, housing 109 basalt rock-cut Kanheri Caves and Vihar & Tulsi lakes.

questions.q: Indravati (Kutru) National Park in Bijapur district of Chhattisgarh provides the primary state haven for which endangered animal, the state animal of Chhattisgarh?
questions.explanation: Indravati National Park along the Indravati River is renowned for conserving one of the last wild populations of the endangered Wild Water Buffalo, the state animal of Chhattisgarh.

questions.q: Kanger Ghati National Park in Bastar district of Chhattisgarh is famous for Tirathgarh waterfall and which subterranean limestone cave containing blind cavefish and stalagmites?
questions.explanation: Kotumsar Cave in Kanger Valley National Park is a 330-meter-deep limestone cave with subterranean stalactites, stalagmites, and the endemic blind cavefish (Indoreonectes evezardi).

questions.q: Simlipal National Park in Mayurbhanj district of Odisha is globally unique as the world's only natural wild reserve harboring which rare variant of Bengal Tiger?
questions.explanation: Simlipal National Park and Biosphere Reserve in Odisha is the only habitat on Earth where pseudo-melanistic (black-striped) tigers exist in the wild, caused by a genetic mutation in the Taqpep gene.

questions.q: Bhitarkanika National Park in Kendrapara district of Odisha is the second largest mangrove ecosystem in India and holds the Guinness World Record for the largest living specimens of which reptile?
questions.explanation: Bhitarkanika's Brahmani-Baitarani delta estuarine network is home to over 1,700 giant Saltwater Crocodiles (some exceeding 20 feet) and borders Gahirmatha, the world's largest Olive Ridley sea turtle nesting beach.

questions.q: Sundarbans National Park in West Bengal, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and Biosphere Reserve, is named after which dominant halophytic mangrove tree species?
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans mangrove forest in the Ganges delta is named after the prolific Sundari tree (Heritiera fomes), celebrated for pneumatophore roots and swimming Bengal Tigers.

questions.q: Manas National Park in Assam, contiguous with the Royal Manas National Park in Bhutan along the Manas River, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site noted for conserving which critically endangered diminutive mammal?
questions.explanation: Manas National Park is a biodiversity hotspot protecting endemic fauna including the world's rarest suid (Pygmy Hog), Golden Langur, Hispid Hare, and Wild Water Buffalo.

questions.q: Nameri National Park in Sonitpur district of Assam, drained by the Jia-Bhoroli River, is celebrated as a prime habitat for which state bird of Assam?
questions.explanation: Nameri National Park in the Himalayan foothills shares its northern border with Pakhui/Pakke Tiger Reserve of Arunachal Pradesh and is famous for the endangered White-winged Wood Duck and Golden Mahseer angling.

questions.q: Which river island national park in Assam, bounded by the Brahmaputra, Lohit, and Dibru rivers, is world-famous for its free-ranging wild feral horses?
questions.explanation: Dibru-Saikhowa National Park in Tinsukia/Dibrugarh is a riverine biome harboring feral horses (descendants of World War II military army horses) and Gangetic river dolphins.

questions.q: Namdapha National Park in Changlang district of Arunachal Pradesh is the only national park in the world that shelters which four apex feline predator species in a single ecosystem?
options: Tiger, Leopard, Snow Leopard, Clouded Leopard
questions.explanation: Namdapha's dramatic altitudinal span (200 m to 4,571 m at Daphabum) enables it to host four big cat species: Bengal Tiger, Common Indian Leopard, Snow Leopard, and Clouded Leopard.

questions.q: Mouling National Park, forming the western part of the Dihang-Dibang Biosphere Reserve in Arunachal Pradesh, is drained by which major trans-boundary river?
questions.explanation: Mouling National Park in Upper Siang district is drained by the Siang River, protecting red pandas, takins, and serows across temperate rainforests.

questions.q: In Manipur's Keibul Lamjao National Park on Loktak Lake, what is the official conservation status of the endemic Eld's Deer (Sangai) that treads upon the floating phumdis?
options: Endangered (Schedule I of Wildlife Protection Act, 1972)
questions.explanation: The Sangai or Manipur brow-antlered dancing deer is critically endangered, protected under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, exclusively found at Keibul Lamjao.

questions.q: Eravikulam National Park in Idukki district of Kerala protects the largest surviving wild population of the endangered Nilgiri Tahr and contains which highest mountain peak of Peninsular India (2,695 m)?
questions.explanation: Anamudi Peak (2,695 meters), the highest peak in India south of the Himalayas, stands inside Eravikulam National Park among rolling montane grassland-shola ecosystems.

questions.q: Silent Valley National Park in the Nilgiri Hills of Palakkad district, Kerala, is drained by which crystal-clear perennial river that was the center of India's historic hydro-electric conservation battle?
questions.explanation: The Kunthipuzha River traverses the entire 24 km length of Silent Valley, saved from a dam project by the pioneering "Save Silent Valley" environmental movement to protect the Lion-tailed Macaque.

questions.q: Which historic 1895 gravity dam on the Periyar River formed the scenic 26 sq km reservoir around which Periyar National Park in Kerala was developed?
questions.explanation: The reservoir formed by the Mullaperiyar Dam in 1895 created the artificial lake habitat that became the Nellikkampatty Game Sanctuary in 1934 and Periyar National Park in 1982.

questions.q: Mudumalai National Park in Nilgiris district of Tamil Nadu shares interstate borders with Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary in Kerala and which tiger reserve in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Mudumalai, Bandipur (Karnataka), and Wayanad (Kerala) meet at the Nilgiri Biosphere tri-junction, creating India's single largest contiguous landscape for Asian Elephants and Royal Bengal Tigers.

questions.q: The Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park along the coast of Tamil Nadu spans 21 uninhabited coral islands and is India's prime reserve for which herbivorous marine mammal?
questions.explanation: The Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park protects extensive shallow seagrass beds that sustain the vulnerable Dugong (sea cow) and over 117 hard coral species between Dhanushkodi and Tuticorin.

questions.q: Which National Park in North Andaman Island encompasses Saddle Peak (732 m) and is drained by the Kalpong River, the only river flowing through the Andaman & Nicobar archipelago?
questions.explanation: Saddle Peak National Park surrounds the highest point in the Andaman & Nicobar Islands (Saddle Peak, 732 m) and is nourished by the Kalpong River, the islands' only freshwater river (site of Kalpong Hydroelectric Project).

questions.q: Madhav National Park (Madhya Pradesh) lies in which district?
questions.explanation: Madhav National Park is in Shivpuri district, Madhya Pradesh. Historic Sakhya Sagar lake.

questions.q: Which legendary conservationist and hunter-turned-naturalist played a pivotal role in establishing Dudhwa as a National Park in Uttar Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Billy Arjan Singh was the driving force behind saving Dudhwa and its swamp deer and tigers.

questions.q: Nanda Devi National Park (Uttarakhand) lies in which district?
questions.explanation: Nanda Devi National Park is in Chamoli district, Uttarakhand. UNESCO peak sanctuary around Nanda Devi.

questions.q: Which endangered pheasant species and state bird of Nagaland can be found in the undisturbed canopies of Intanki?
questions.explanation: Blyth's Tragopan (Tragopan blythii) is the state bird of Nagaland and inhabits its montane forests.

questions.q: The historic Chiran Palace and its surrounding pristine woodlands form which National Park in Telangana?
questions.explanation: Chiran Palace complex in Jubilee Hills forms Kasu Brahmananda Reddy (KBR) National Park.

questions.q: The spectacular Barehipani Falls (tiered 399m) and Joranda Falls are located within which National Park of Odisha?
questions.explanation: Barehipani and Joranda waterfalls are prominent landmarks of Similipal National Park.

questions.q: Keoladeo Ghana National Park is located in which state or union territory?
questions.explanation: Keoladeo Ghana National Park is in Bharatpur district, Rajasthan. UNESCO World Heritage wetland bird sanctuary.

questions.q: Which national park in Madhya Pradesh matches this description: "Famous for Hardground Barasingha"?
questions.explanation: Kanha National Park is in Mandla & Balaghat districts, Madhya Pradesh. Famous for Hardground Barasingha.

questions.q: Kuno National Park is located in which state or union territory?
questions.explanation: Kuno National Park is in Sheopur district, Madhya Pradesh. Site of Project Cheetah reintroduction.

questions.q: Inderkilla National Park (Himachal Pradesh) lies in which district?
questions.explanation: Inderkilla National Park is in Kullu district, Himachal Pradesh. High altitude Himalayan wildlife sanctuary.

questions.q: Which river drainage basin encompasses the lowland semi-evergreen forests of Intanki National Park in Nagaland?
questions.explanation: Intanki is drained by the Dhansiri river system flowing towards the Brahmaputra.

questions.q: Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park (Tamil Nadu) lies in which district?
questions.explanation: Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park is in Ramanathapuram & Thoothukudi districts, Tamil Nadu. First marine biosphere reserve in South Asia.

questions.q: Which swamp-dwelling deer subspecies was saved from near-extinction in the wet grasslands of Dudhwa, Uttar Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Dudhwa National Park protects the largest surviving population of the northern swamp deer (Rucervus duvaucelii duvaucelii).

questions.q: Keibul Lamjao National Park floats upon which largest freshwater lake of Northeast India?
questions.explanation: Keibul Lamjao forms the southern part of Loktak Lake in Manipur.

questions.q: Which graceful state animal of Punjab, Haryana, and Andhra Pradesh is famously protected in Mahavir Harina Vanasthali, Telangana?
questions.explanation: Mahavir Harina Vanasthali National Park is dedicated to preserving the Blackbuck (Antilope cervicapra).

questions.q: Clouded Leopard National Park (Tripura) lies in which district?
questions.explanation: Clouded Leopard National Park is in Sipahijala district, Tripura. Dedicated sanctuary for the elusive Clouded Leopard.

questions.q: Gahirmatha beach adjacent to Bhitarkanika in Odisha is celebrated globally as the world's largest nesting ground for which creature?
questions.explanation: Gahirmatha beach witnesses massive mass nesting (Arribada) of Olive Ridley sea turtles.

questions.q: Mollem National Park in Goa forms a critical ecological corridor in which UNESCO World Heritage mountain chain?
questions.explanation: Mollem National Park lies in the lush tropical rainforest belt of the Western Ghats.

questions.q: The majestic multi-tiered Dudhsagar Waterfalls is located on which river inside Mollem National Park, Goa?
questions.explanation: Dudhsagar Falls is on the Mandovi River along the Goa-Karnataka border in Mollem NP.

questions.q: Which national park in Assam matches this description: "Mini-Kaziranga on northern bank of Brahmaputra"?
questions.explanation: Rajiv Gandhi Orang National Park is in Darrang & Sonitpur districts, Assam. Mini-Kaziranga on northern bank of Brahmaputra.

questions.q: The historic 12th-century basalt Tambdi Surla Mahadev temple is preserved inside which protected area of Goa?
questions.explanation: The Kadamba-era Tambdi Surla temple is located deep inside Mollem National Park.

questions.q: Which national park in Odisha matches this description: "Second largest mangrove ecosystem in India; Saltwater crocodiles"?
questions.explanation: Bhitarkanika National Park is in Kendrapara district, Odisha. Second largest mangrove ecosystem in India; Saltwater crocodiles.

questions.q: Which national park in Tamil Nadu matches this description: "First national park in South India (part of Nilgiri Biosphere)"?
options: Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park
questions.explanation: Mudumalai National Park is in Nilgiris district, Tamil Nadu. First national park in South India (part of Nilgiri Biosphere).

questions.q: Which national park in Andaman & Nicobar Islands matches this description: "Part of Great Nicobar Biosphere Reserve"?
questions.explanation: Campbell Bay National Park is in Great Nicobar district, Andaman & Nicobar Islands. Part of Great Nicobar Biosphere Reserve.

questions.q: Which critically endangered deer species, the state animal of Manipur known as the "dancing deer", is endemic to Keibul Lamjao?
questions.explanation: The Sangai or dancing deer is found exclusively on the phumdis of Keibul Lamjao National Park.

questions.q: Which magnificent wild sheep with giant curved horns and the world's largest wild sheep species is conserved in Hemis, Ladakh?
questions.explanation: The Great Tibetan Sheep (Ovis ammon hodgsoni), or Argali, is protected in the high valleys of Hemis.

questions.q: Papikonda National Park is located in which state or union territory?
questions.explanation: Papikonda National Park is in East & West Godavari districts, Andhra Pradesh. Spans the scenic Papi Hills on Godavari River.

questions.q: Which national park in Nagaland matches this description: "Habitat of the Hoolock Gibbon and Great Indian Hornbill"?
questions.explanation: Intanki (Ntangki) National Park is in Peren district, Nagaland. Habitat of the Hoolock Gibbon and Great Indian Hornbill.

questions.q: Chandoli National Park (Maharashtra) lies in which district?
questions.explanation: Chandoli National Park is in Sangli, Satara & Kolhapur districts, Maharashtra. Sahyadri Tiger Reserve core.

questions.q: Which national park in West Bengal matches this description: "Largest population of One-Horned Rhinos in Bengal"?
questions.explanation: Jaldapara National Park is in Alipurduar district, West Bengal. Largest population of One-Horned Rhinos in Bengal.

questions.q: Which legendary trans-Himalayan river bounds Hemis National Park to the north in Ladakh?
questions.explanation: The Indus River flows along the northern boundary of Hemis National Park.

questions.q: Which famous ornithologist helped establish Sultanpur in Haryana as a notified bird sanctuary in 1972?
questions.explanation: Peter Scott along with Indira Gandhi helped establish Sultanpur Lake Sanctuary in 1972.

questions.q: Mouling National Park is located in which state or union territory?
questions.explanation: Mouling National Park is in Upper Siang district, Arunachal Pradesh. Siang River biodiversity canyon.

questions.q: Kalesar National Park (Haryana) lies in which district?
questions.explanation: Kalesar National Park is in Yamunanagar district, Haryana. Shivalik sal forests along Yamuna River.

questions.q: Sundarbans National Park is located in which state or union territory?
questions.explanation: Sundarbans National Park is in South 24 Parganas district, West Bengal. World’s largest mangrove forest and Royal Bengal Tiger habitat.

questions.q: Which national park in Assam matches this description: "UNESCO Natural World Heritage site along Bhutan border"?
questions.explanation: Manas National Park is in Baksa & Chirang districts, Assam. UNESCO Natural World Heritage site along Bhutan border.

questions.q: Rajiv Gandhi (Rameswaram) National Park (Andhra Pradesh) lies in which district?
questions.explanation: Rajiv Gandhi (Rameswaram) National Park is in YSR Kadapa district, Andhra Pradesh. Pristine peninsular biodiversity reserve.

questions.q: Rajiv Gandhi (Rameswaram) National Park is situated along the Penna River in which state?
questions.explanation: Rajiv Gandhi (Rameswaram) National Park is located in YSR Kadapa district of Andhra Pradesh.

questions.q: Marine (Gulf of Kutch) National Park (Gujarat) lies in which district?
questions.explanation: Marine (Gulf of Kutch) National Park is in Jamnagar & Devbhumi Dwarka districts, Gujarat. India’s first marine national park.

questions.q: Which national park in Madhya Pradesh matches this description: "Setting for Kipling's The Jungle Book"?
questions.explanation: Pench National Park is in Seoni & Chhindwara districts, Madhya Pradesh. Setting for Kipling's The Jungle Book.

questions.q: Sri Venkateswara National Park forms the core of which Biosphere Reserve in Andhra Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Sri Venkateswara National Park is the core zone of the Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve, designated in 2010.

questions.q: India's very first Marine National Park was established in which coastal region of Gujarat?
questions.explanation: Marine National Park was established in 1982 in the Gulf of Kutch near Jamnagar, Gujarat.

questions.q: Which rare melanistic big cat is occasionally sighted in the dense canopies of Mollem National Park, Goa?
questions.explanation: Black Panthers (melanistic leopards) are documented inhabitants of Mollem's dense evergreen forests.

questions.q: Rajbari (Bison) National Park is located in which state or union territory?
questions.explanation: Rajbari (Bison) National Park is in South Tripura (Trishna) district, Tripura. Protected habitat for Indian Gaur (Bison).

questions.q: Kasu Brahmananda Reddy (KBR) National Park is located in which state or union territory?
questions.explanation: Kasu Brahmananda Reddy (KBR) National Park is in Hyderabad district, Telangana. Urban forest park in Jubilee Hills, Hyderabad.

questions.q: Namdapha National Park in Arunachal Pradesh is unique on Earth for sheltering which four big cat species within a single reserve?
options: Snow Leopard, Caracal, Lynx, and Leopard
Tiger, Common Leopard, Clouded Leopard, and Snow Leopard
questions.explanation: Namdapha spans an elevation range from 200m to 4,500m, allowing tropical tigers, clouded leopards, common leopards, and alpine snow leopards to coexist.

questions.q: Which national park in Andaman & Nicobar Islands matches this description: "Smallest National Park in India (only 0.03 sq km)"?
questions.explanation: South Button Island National Park is in South Andaman district, Andaman & Nicobar Islands. Smallest National Park in India (only 0.03 sq km).

questions.q: In which district of northwestern Bihar is Valmiki National Park situated?
questions.explanation: Valmiki National Park is in the West Champaran district bordering Nepal.

questions.q: Which deltaic river confluence creates the fertile mangrove wetlands of Bhitarkanika National Park in Odisha?
questions.explanation: Bhitarkanika is formed by the delta of Brahmani, Baitarani, and Dhamra rivers in Kendrapara.

questions.q: Which river flows through the northern part of Betla National Park in Jharkhand?
questions.explanation: The North Koel River and its tributaries flow through Betla National Park.

questions.q: Phawngpui Blue Mountain National Park is located in which state or union territory?
questions.explanation: Phawngpui Blue Mountain National Park is in Lawngtlai district, Mizoram. Protects Mizoram's highest peak (Blue Mountain).

questions.q: Desert National Park (Rajasthan) lies in which district?
questions.explanation: Desert National Park is in Jaisalmer & Barmer districts, Rajasthan. Great Indian Bustard sanctuary in Thar Desert.

questions.q: Valmiki National Park is located in which state or union territory?
questions.explanation: Valmiki National Park is in West Champaran district, Bihar. Contiguous with Chitwan National Park of Nepal along Gandak River.

questions.q: Clouded Leopard National Park was carved out of which existing protected wildlife sanctuary in Tripura?
questions.explanation: Clouded Leopard National Park covers a portion of Sipahijala Wildlife Sanctuary.

questions.q: Which national park in Madhya Pradesh matches this description: "Part of Sanjay-Dubri Tiger Reserve"?
questions.explanation: Sanjay National Park is in Sidhi district, Madhya Pradesh. Part of Sanjay-Dubri Tiger Reserve.

questions.q: Indira Gandhi (Anamalai) National Park is located in which state or union territory?

questions.q: Which launch vehicle of ISRO successfully launched Chandrayaan-3 into translunar orbit prior to its historic soft landing near the lunar south pole?

questions.q: The PM Vishwakarma Scheme provides holistic end-to-end support, subsidized credit of up to ₹3 lakh, and modern toolkit incentives for traditional artisans across how many recognized trades?

questions.q: Who serves as the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) of India, functioning as the Permanent Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee?

questions.q: Under the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) approved by the Union Cabinet, which site was selected for setting up India's first commercial semiconductor fabrication facility (Fab) by Tata Electronics and Powerchip (PSMC)?

questions.q: What is the name of the female humanoid robot developed by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) to fly aboard uncrewed test missions of the Gaganyaan human spaceflight programme?
questions.explanation: Vyommitra ("Space Friend") is a half-humanoid robot developed by ISRO. Equipped with artificial intelligence and speech capabilities, she is programmed to monitor environmental parameters, operate control panels, and simulate human physiological responses during Gaganyaan uncrewed test flights.

questions.q: Under the PM-Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana launched with an outlay of ₹75,021 crore, how many units of free electricity per month are targeted for 1 crore beneficiary households?

questions.q: The Union Cabinet approved the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) for Central Government employees. What percentage of the average basic pay drawn in the last 12 months is guaranteed as assured pension for qualifying service of minimum 25 years?

questions.explanation: UNESCO was founded in 1945 and its permanent international headquarters is located in Place de Fontenoy, Paris, France.

questions.q: On 25 July 2026, which historic sacred Buddhist landscape in Uttar Pradesh was officially inscribed as India's 45th UNESCO World Heritage Site under cultural criteria?
questions.explanation: Sarnath in Uttar Pradesh was officially inscribed on 25 July 2026 as India's 45th UNESCO World Heritage Site, bringing India's total World Heritage properties to 45.

questions.q: What is the exact official category breakdown of India's 45 UNESCO World Heritage Sites following the 2026 Sarnath inscription?
questions.explanation: With 45 inscribed properties, India's official UNESCO World Heritage portfolio consists of 36 Cultural sites, 8 Natural sites, and 1 Mixed site (Khangchendzonga National Park). India ranks 6th in the world for most World Heritage properties.

questions.q: Which serial nomination comprising 12 strategic hill, coastal, and island forts representing the military genius of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj was recognized as India's 44th World Heritage Site?
questions.explanation: The "Maratha Military Landscapes of India" comprises 12 forts (11 in Maharashtra: Shivneri, Raigad, Torna, Rajgad, Pratapgad, Suvarnadurg, Panhala, Vijaydurg, Sindhudurg, Lohagad, Alibag; and Gingee in Tamil Nadu) exhibiting 17th-century guerrilla warfare strategy and naval defence.

questions.q: Inscribed in 2024 at the 46th Session in New Delhi, the "Moidams" of the Ahom Dynasty in Charaideo, Assam represent which cultural heritage archetype?
options: Monolithic rock-cut temples dedicated to Lord Shiva
Ancient megalithic dolmens and cist burials
Mound-burial system of Ahom royalty and aristocracy
questions.explanation: The Moidams are vaulted earth-and-brick mound-burial tumuli of the Tai-Ahom kings and queens in Charaideo, Assam. Spanning 600 years, they represent a unique pyramidal burial landscape and the first cultural World Heritage Site from Northeast India.

questions.q: In 1983, India had its first properties inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List. Which four sites formed this historic inaugural group?
options: Elephanta Caves, Hampi, Sanchi, and Pattadakal
Sun Temple Konark, Mahabalipuram, Kaziranga, and Manas
Ajanta Caves, Ellora Caves, Agra Fort, and Taj Mahal
Qutb Minar, Humayun's Tomb, Fatehpur Sikri, and Khajuraho
questions.explanation: The inaugural 1983 inscriptions for India were Ajanta Caves (Maharashtra), Ellora Caves (Maharashtra), Agra Fort (Uttar Pradesh), and the Taj Mahal (Uttar Pradesh).

questions.q: Dholavira: a Harappan City, inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 2021, is located on Khadir Bet island in the Great Rann of Kutch (Gujarat). What is its most outstanding engineering feature?
options: A monumental cascading rainwater harvesting and reservoir system
A stone amphitheatre with acoustics for theatrical performances
A massive subterranean Buddhist vihara complex
The world's earliest copper smelting blast furnace
questions.explanation: Dholavira flourished between 3000 BCE and 1500 BCE and is distinguished by its sophisticated stone water management system, comprising 16 interconnected cascading rock-cut reservoirs, check dams, and stormwater drainage channels engineered to survive desert aridity.

questions.q: Kakatiya Rudreshwara (Ramappa) Temple in Palampet, Telangana, inscribed on the UNESCO list in 2021, was celebrated for which distinctive technological innovation?
options: Corbelled granite domes balanced on a single central pivot
Interlocking iron clamps without any lime mortar
Pure marble pillars carved with musical tones
Floating bricks (sponge bricks) and sandbox foundation technology
questions.explanation: The 13th-century Ramappa Temple, built under Kakatiya ruler Recharla Rudra, features ultra-lightweight "floating porous bricks" that reduce weight on the roof, constructed over a seismic-resistant "sandbox foundation" that absorbs earthquake tremors.

questions.q: Inscribed in 2023, which university town and ashram founded by Rabindranath Tagore in Birbhum district of West Bengal is celebrated for its open-air education and international humanism?
questions.explanation: Santiniketan, established by Maharshi Debendranath Tagore in 1863 and transformed by Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore into Visva-Bharati University in 1921, was inscribed in 2023 as an architectural and philosophical embodiment of pan-Asian internationalism and nature-based education.

questions.q: The "Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas", inscribed as India's 42nd World Heritage property in 2023, comprises 12th–13th century stellate (star-shaped) temples in which three Karnataka locations?
questions.explanation: The Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas comprises the Chennakeshava Temple at Belur, the Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebidu, and the Keshava Temple at Somanathapura in Karnataka, famous for their soapstone (chloritic schist) intricate friezes and star-shaped ground plans.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of India's 8 officially inscribed Natural World Heritage Sites?
questions.explanation: Gir National Park in Gujarat is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site. India's 8 Natural World Heritage Sites are: Kaziranga, Manas, Keoladeo, Sundarbans, Nanda Devi & Valley of Flowers, Western Ghats, and Great Himalayan National Park Conservation Area.

questions.q: The Sun Temple at Konark (Odisha), inscribed on the UNESCO list in 1984, was constructed in the 13th century by which ruler of the Eastern Ganga Dynasty?
questions.explanation: The Sun Temple at Konark was built around 1250 CE by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga Dynasty. Conceived as a grand 24-wheeled chariot of Surya drawn by 7 horses, it represents the pinnacle of Kalinga stone architecture.

questions.q: In which year were India's first UNESCO World Heritage Sites inscribed?
questions.explanation: Ajanta Caves, Ellora Caves, Agra Fort and the Taj Mahal were inscribed in 1983.

questions.q: Rani-ki-Vav, the stepwell inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 2014, is located in which town?
questions.explanation: Rani-ki-Vav, built in the 11th century in memory of King Bhima I, is in Patan, Gujarat.

questions.q: Which was India's first city to be inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage City, in 2017?
questions.explanation: The Historic City of Ahmedabad was inscribed in 2017; Jaipur followed in 2019.

questions.q: The Western Ghats were inscribed as a Natural World Heritage Site in which year?
questions.explanation: The Western Ghats were inscribed in 2012 for their outstanding biodiversity and endemism.

questions.q: Which three railways together make up the 'Mountain Railways of India' World Heritage property?
options: Darjeeling Himalayan, Nilgiri Mountain and Kalka-Shimla
Darjeeling Himalayan, Matheran and Kangra Valley
questions.explanation: The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway (1999), Nilgiri Mountain Railway (2005) and Kalka-Shimla Railway (2008) form the property.

questions.q: The Rock Shelters of Bhimbetka, inscribed in 2003, are located in which state?
questions.explanation: Bhimbetka, in Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh, has prehistoric rock paintings.

questions.q: Which architect designed the Capitol Complex at Chandigarh, part of a transnational World Heritage inscription in 2016?
questions.explanation: The Capitol Complex is part of 'The Architectural Work of Le Corbusier', inscribed in 2016.

questions.q: Which group of forts was inscribed in 2013 as 'Hill Forts of ___'?
questions.explanation: The Hill Forts of Rajasthan include Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore, Gagron, Amber and Jaisalmer.

questions.q: The Great Himalayan National Park Conservation Area, inscribed in 2014, is located in which state?
questions.explanation: The Great Himalayan National Park is in Kullu district, Himachal Pradesh.

questions.q: Which UNESCO body meets every year to decide on new inscriptions to the World Heritage List?
options: International Council on Monuments and Sites
questions.explanation: The 21-member World Heritage Committee decides inscriptions; ICOMOS and IUCN act as advisory bodies.

questions.q: What is India's official nomination dossier for the 2024–2025 cycle from its UNESCO Tentative List, showcasing forts such as Raigad, Shivneri, and Sindhudurg?
options: Maratha Military Landscapes of India (Maharashtra & Tamil Nadu)
questions.explanation: India nominated the "Maratha Military Landscapes of India" (12 components across Maharashtra and Gingee in Tamil Nadu) developed between the 17th and 19th centuries under Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj and successors.

questions.q: According to the Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention, a State Party can submit a nomination for World Heritage inscription only if the site has been on its Tentative List for at least:
questions.explanation: Paragraph 65 of the UNESCO Operational Guidelines mandates that a property must be included on the State Party's official Tentative List for at least one year before submitting the formal nomination dossier.

questions.q: Which hilltop fortress in Madhya Pradesh, referred to by Mughal Emperor Babur as "the pearl among gems of the fortresses of Hind", is on India's UNESCO Tentative List?
questions.explanation: Gwalior Fort, constructed upon an isolated sandstone hill with the famous Man Mandir Palace and turquoise glazed tile architecture, is on India's Tentative List.

questions.q: Khooni Bhandara, a unique underground qanat water management system constructed in the 17th century by Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khana, submitted to the Tentative List, is located in which city of Madhya Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Khooni Bhandara in Burhanpur, MP, is a sophisticated subterranean Persian qanat water supply network drawing underground spring water through gravity pipelines without mechanical pumps.

questions.q: The 11th-century Sun Temple at Modhera on the banks of River Pushpavati, built during the reign of King Bhima I of the Chaulukya/Solanki dynasty, is located in which district of Gujarat?
questions.explanation: The Sun Temple at Modhera in Mehsana district of Gujarat, with its ornate Surya Kund (stepped reservoir) and Sabha Mandap, is submitted on India's Tentative List.

questions.q: Vadnagar in Mehsana district of Gujarat, submitted to the Tentative List as a multi-layered historic town, is globally significant for continuous urban habitation dating back to:
options: 8th Century BCE (over 2,700 years of continuous habitation)
questions.explanation: Excavations by ASI reveal Vadnagar as a rare fortified living historic town with continuous settlement across Mauryan, Indo-Greek, Kshatrapa, Solanki, and Sultanate periods spanning over 2,700 years.

questions.q: Prehistoric laterite plateaus in the Konkan region containing thousands of open-air rock petroglyphs depicting animals, humans, and geometric patterns are on the Tentative List across which two states?
questions.explanation: The "Geoglyphs of Konkan Region" spanning Ratnagiri/Sindhudurg in Maharashtra and neighbouring Goa represent remarkable Mesolithic rock engravings carved into laterite plateaus.

questions.q: Under UNESCO nomination criteria, what does Criterion (i) represent for a cultural property nominated to the Tentative and World Heritage List?
options: Exceptional testimony to a cultural tradition
Important interchange of human values over a span of time
Outstanding example of a traditional human settlement
questions.explanation: UNESCO Criterion (i) requires a property to "represent a masterpiece of human creative genius". There are 6 cultural criteria (i–vi) and 4 natural criteria (vii–x).

questions.q: What is the fundamental legal distinction between a site on a country's UNESCO Tentative List versus an inscribed World Heritage Site?
options: Tentative List sites already have international treaty protection
Tentative List is an inventory of prospective sites; only inscribed sites have official World Heritage status
Tentative List sites receive direct funding from the UN
Tentative List sites cannot be visited by the public
questions.explanation: A Tentative List is an inventory of heritage properties that a State Party intends to consider for nomination in subsequent years. Inclusion on the Tentative List does not confer World Heritage status or legal protection under the 1972 Convention until formally inscribed by the Committee.

questions.q: Which nodal government organization in India is responsible for preparing and submitting nomination dossiers and managing India's UNESCO Tentative List submissions?
options: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), Ministry of Culture
Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage (INTACH)
questions.explanation: The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) under the Ministry of Culture serves as the nodal agency of the Government of India for all matters relating to the UNESCO World Heritage Convention.

questions.q: Which island in the Andaman and Nicobar archipelago was added to India's UNESCO Tentative List for its exceptional Karst-mud-volcano complex and limestone caves?
questions.explanation: The Karst-mud-volcano Complex of Baratang Island in the Andaman & Nicobar Islands is on India's UNESCO Tentative List. It exhibits active mud volcano degassing vents, subaerial karst limestone cave formations, and coastal mangrove waterways.

questions.q: The "Andaman Subduction Volcanoes" on the UNESCO Tentative List consists of Barren Island and which dormant volcanic island that is also the sole habitat of an endangered endemic hornbill?
questions.explanation: The serial nomination includes Barren Island (India's only active volcano) and Narcondam Island (a dormant volcanic island formed by subduction of the Indo-Australian plate, sole home to the endemic Narcondam hornbill Rhyticeros narcondami).

questions.q: The Sirpur Cultural and Archaeological Landscape, included on India's UNESCO Tentative List, is an ancient capital of the Sarabhapuriya and Somavamshi dynasties along which river in Chhattisgarh?
questions.explanation: Sirpur (ancient Shripura) in Mahasamund district of Chhattisgarh lies along the Mahanadi River. It flourished between the 5th and 12th centuries as a major Buddhist, Shaiva, and Vaishnava centre, featuring the 7th-century brick Lakshmana Temple and Teevardev Mahavihar.

questions.q: The serial nomination "The Sites of Satyagraha, India's Non-violent Freedom Movement" on the UNESCO Tentative List commemorates Mahatma Gandhi's ashrams and campaign landmarks. Which of the following sites is NOT in Gujarat?
questions.explanation: Sevagram Ashram is located near Wardha in Maharashtra, where Mahatma Gandhi resided from 1936 until his death in 1948. Sabarmati, Kochrab, and Dandi are situated in Gujarat.

questions.q: The rock-cut Bagh Cave paintings, included on India's UNESCO Tentative List, are situated on the banks of the Baghani river in which district of Madhya Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Bagh Caves comprise nine rock-cut Buddhist sanctuaries in Dhar district of Madhya Pradesh, renowned for their 5th–6th century CE classical murals and tempera wall paintings executed in the same Gupta-period aesthetic tradition as Ajanta.

questions.q: Ginnorgarh Fort on the UNESCO Tentative List, situated in the Vindhyan hills near Sehore in Madhya Pradesh, was the historic stronghold of which legendary 18th-century Gond queen?
questions.explanation: Ginnorgarh Fort in Sehore district of Madhya Pradesh is a medieval hill fortress surrounded by deep ravines. It served as the capital of the Gond kingdom under King Nizam Shah and his consort Rani Kamlapati.

questions.q: The "Chambal Valley Temple Group" on the UNESCO Tentative List includes the spectacular restored cluster of over 200 Gurjara-Pratihara temples at which site in Morena district, Madhya Pradesh?
questions.explanation: The Bateshwar Temple complex near Morena in the Chambal valley comprises over 200 sandstone temples built between the 8th and 10th centuries by the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty, painstakingly reconstructed by archaeologist K.K. Muhammed of the ASI.

questions.q: The Udaigiri Caves near Vidisha (Madhya Pradesh), nominated on the UNESCO Tentative List, feature Cave 5 with which monumental Gupta-period high-relief rock sculpture?
options: Colossal Varaha Avatar rescuing Prithvi (Earth Goddess)
questions.explanation: Cave 5 at Udaigiri features the iconic 5th-century Gupta-era colossal rock sculpture of Varaha (the boar incarnation of Lord Vishnu) lifting the Earth Goddess Bhudevi from the cosmic waters, symbolizing royal protection and restoration of cosmic order under Chandragupta II.

questions.q: The "Rangpur-Sivasagar Historic Ensemble" on the UNESCO Tentative List showcases the architectural legacy of the Ahom dynasty in Assam. Which building served as Asia's earliest surviving royal amphitheatre?
questions.explanation: Rang Ghar ("House of Entertainment") in Sivasagar, Assam is a two-storeyed oval brick pavilion built by Ahom King Pramatta Singha in 1744. It is widely considered one of the earliest surviving outdoor amphitheatres in Asia, used by royalty to view buffalo fights and Bihu dances.

questions.q: Which semi-arid region in northern Rajasthan is nominated on the UNESCO Tentative List as "The Painted Haveli Towns", famed for thousands of 18th-to-20th-century frescoed merchant mansions?
questions.explanation: Shekhawati comprising towns in Jhunjhunu, Sikar, and Churu districts (Mandawa, Nawalgarh, Fatehpur, Ramgarh) is renowned as the world's largest "open-air art gallery", featuring thousands of ornate havelis covered in vibrant narrative frescoes depicting mythological, social, and British colonial themes.

questions.q: The UNESCO Tentative List proposal "Nicobarese Cultural Continuity" honors the living indigenous architecture and heritage of the Nicobarese. What is the traditional circular dome-shaped wooden house on stilts called?
questions.explanation: The traditional stilted circular beehive house of the Nicobarese tribe is called a Pati or Tuhet. Raised on wooden pilings 2–3 meters above ground to protect against tides and pests, it demonstrates centuries of indigenous architectural adaptation to maritime and seismic conditions.

questions.q: The "Colonial Penal Settlement of Andaman Islands" on the UNESCO Tentative List includes which iconic three-storeyed panopticon brick prison where Indian freedom fighters were sentenced to "Kala Pani"?
questions.explanation: Cellular Jail in Port Blair, constructed between 1896 and 1906, was a seven-winged panopticon fortress designed for solitary confinement where thousands of Indian independence activists and revolutionaries were exiled under brutal conditions.

questions.q: In which year did India ratify the UNESCO World Heritage Convention?
questions.explanation: The Convention was adopted in 1972 and India ratified it in 1977.

questions.q: The 'Living Root Bridges' (Jingkieng Jri) added to India's Tentative List in 2022 are found in which state?
questions.explanation: The living root bridges are grown by Khasi and Jaintia communities in Meghalaya.

questions.q: Majuli, on India's Tentative List, is best described as which of the following?
options: A river island in the Brahmaputra known for Vaishnavite sattras
A coastal mangrove forest in Odisha
questions.explanation: Majuli in Assam is a large river island and the centre of neo-Vaishnavite sattra culture.

questions.q: The Apatani Cultural Landscape on India's Tentative List is located in which valley?
questions.explanation: The Apatani tribe practise integrated rice-fish cultivation in the Ziro Valley.

questions.q: Sri Harmandir Sahib, on India's Tentative List, is located in which city?
questions.explanation: Sri Harmandir Sahib (the Golden Temple) is in Amritsar, Punjab.

questions.q: Which advisory body evaluates cultural sites nominated to the World Heritage List?
questions.explanation: ICOMOS (International Council on Monuments and Sites) evaluates cultural nominations; IUCN evaluates natural ones.

questions.q: How many selection criteria in total does UNESCO use for inscription on the World Heritage List?
questions.explanation: There are ten criteria: (i)–(vi) cultural and (vii)–(x) natural.

questions.q: The 'Temples at Bishnupur', known for terracotta architecture and on the Tentative List, are in which state?
questions.explanation: The Malla-era terracotta temples of Bishnupur are in Bankura district, West Bengal.

questions.q: How many classical dance forms are officially recognized by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's national academy of music, dance, and drama?
questions.explanation: The Sangeet Natak Akademi recognizes 8 Indian Classical Dance forms: Bharatanatyam (TN), Kathak (UP), Kathakali (Kerala), Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Kuchipudi (AP), and Sattriya (Assam).

questions.q: Sattriya classical dance, originating in the Sattras (monasteries) of Assam, was introduced in the 15th century by which revered Bhakti saint and reformer?
questions.explanation: Sattriya was introduced in Assam by the great 15th-century Vaishnavite saint-reformer Mahapurusha Srimanta Sankardev as a sacred theatrical devotional medium in monastic Sattras, recognized as classical by SNA in 2000.

questions.q: Bharatanatyam, historically performed in temples by Devadasis under names like Sadir Attam and Dasi Attam, originated in which southern state?
questions.explanation: Bharatanatyam is the oldest classical dance tradition of Tamil Nadu, codified in Bharata's Natya Shastra and revived in the modern era by Rukmini Devi Arundale and E. Krishna Iyer.

questions.q: Which graceful classical dance of Kerala, known as the "Dance of the Enchantress", is performed solo by women wearing white or cream kasavu sarees with gold borders?
questions.explanation: Mohiniyattam is characterized by delicate Lasya movements, swaying torso rhythms, and white/cream gold-bordered kasavu costumes, drawing from the mythological enchantress avatar of Lord Vishnu (Mohini).

questions.q: Pandit Birju Maharaj, who passed away in 2022, was a legendary doyen and torchbearer of which gharana of Kathak classical dance?
questions.explanation: Pandit Birju Maharaj belonged to the illustrious Kalka-Bindadin family of Lucknow Gharana, renowned for sublime abhinaya (expression), lightning footwork (tatkar), and chakkars (spins).

questions.q: Which distinguished master is universally celebrated for reviving, systematizing, and internationally popularizing Odissi classical dance in the 20th century?
questions.explanation: Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra, the first recipient of the Padma Vibhushan from Odisha, revived the Gotipua and Mahari traditions to establish Odissi on global concert stages.

questions.q: Bihu, characterized by energetic brisk steps and rapid hand movements performed to the rhythmic beats of the dhol, pepa, and toka, is the quintessential folk dance of which state?
questions.explanation: Bihu is the most popular folk dance of Assam, performed during Bohag Bihu (Rongali Bihu) in mid-April to celebrate the Assamese New Year and sowing season.

questions.q: Which traditional folk dance form of Gujarat, performed in concentric circles around a clay lantern during the nine nights of Navratri, was inscribed in 2023 on UNESCO's Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage?
questions.explanation: Garba of Gujarat was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in December 2023 at the 18th session of the Intergovernmental Committee in Botswana.

questions.q: Cheraw, commonly known as the "Bamboo Dance" where male dancers rhythmically clap bamboo staves on the ground while female dancers step in and out of the grids, belongs to which state?
questions.explanation: Cheraw is the traditional bamboo dance of Mizoram, performed during festivals like Chapchar Kut, involving intricate coordination and timing between dancers and bamboo holders.

questions.q: Kalbelia folk songs and dances, celebrated for serpentine swirling movements to the poongi/been by women of the nomadic snake-charmer community, belongs to which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Kalbelia is a folk dance of Rajasthan performed by the Kalbelia community, recognized by UNESCO on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

questions.q: Which energetic spring harvest festival dance of Assam is performed by young men and women in traditional Muga silk attire, accompanied by the Pepa (buffalo horn flute) and Dhol?
questions.explanation: Bihu is the quintessential folk dance of Assam, celebrated during Rongali (Bohag) Bihu to mark the Assamese New Year and sowing season. It is characterized by brisk steps, rapid hand movements, and swaying of the hips accompanied by the dhol and pepa.

questions.q: Which martial and folk dance tradition of Eastern India (inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage) is practiced in three distinct regional sub-styles: Purulia, Seraikella, and Mayurbhanj?
questions.explanation: Chhau is a semi-classical martial dance of Eastern India. Purulia Chhau (West Bengal) and Seraikella Chhau (Jharkhand) utilize elaborate painted masks depicting mythological figures, while Mayurbhanj Chhau (Odisha) is performed without masks.

questions.q: The Kalbelia dance, inscribed on the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2010, is a sensuous serpent-like folk dance traditionally performed by women of which nomadic community in Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: Kalbelia is a folk dance performed by women of the Kalbelia snake-charmer community in Rajasthan. Dressed in flowing black embroidered skirts (ghaghra) resembling serpent scales, they swirl to the music of the Pungi (been), dafli, and khanjari.

questions.q: Yakshagana is a traditional theatre-dance form combining stylized dance, Carnatic-raga singing, extempore dialogue, and towering headgear (kedage), native to which southern state?
questions.explanation: Yakshagana is a vibrant folk theatre and dance tradition native to coastal and Malenadu districts of Karnataka (Udupi, Dakshina Kannada, Uttara Kannada). Staged through the night, it dramatizes episodes from the Mahabharata, Ramayana, and Bhagavata Purana.

questions.q: Which energetic and rhythmically rapid folk dance of Maharashtra, performed to the beats of the Dholki by female dancers wearing a nine-yard Nauvari saree, is an integral element of traditional Tamasha theatre?
questions.explanation: Lavani is the quintessential traditional musical folk dance of Maharashtra, originating from the Marathi word "Lavanya" (beauty). Performed to the brisk, syncopated rhythms of the dholki in a nine-yard Nauvari saree, it flourished under the Peshwa court in the 18th century.

questions.q: Which traditional celebratory folk dance of Jammu and Kashmir is performed exclusively by women facing each other in linked rows during Eid, Ramzan, and the spring harvest season?
questions.explanation: Rouf is a lyrical and graceful women's folk dance of the Kashmir Valley. Women form two parallel facing rows with arms linked across each other's waists and glide forward and backward in unison to melodic Kashmiri folk songs.

questions.q: Ghoomar is a graceful pirouetting traditional folk dance performed by veiled women in flowing skirts, originally developed by which tribal community in Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: Ghoomar originates from the Bhil tribe of Rajasthan, who originally danced it in reverence to Goddess Saraswati. Later adopted by Rajput royal courts, it became renowned for graceful swirling movements (Ghoomna) displaying the wide flares of the colorful ghaghra.

questions.q: Koodiyattam, a 2,000-year-old Sanskrit temple drama tradition of Kerala proclaimed by UNESCO as a Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity in 2001, is accompanied by which copper percussion drum?
questions.explanation: Koodiyattam is the world's oldest surviving Sanskrit theatre tradition, staged in traditional temple theatres called Koothambalams in Kerala. It is accompanied primarily by the Mizhavu, a large sacred copper drum played exclusively with the bare palms by members of the Ambalavasi Nambiar community.

questions.q: Thang-Ta is a traditional martial art and dance form native to Manipur, practiced by the Meitei community. What do the words "Thang" and "Ta" specifically denote?
questions.explanation: Thang-Ta (officially known as Huyen Langlon) is the ancient martial art tradition of Manipur. "Thang" means sword and "Ta" means spear. It integrates armed combat techniques with devotional rhythmic movements dedicated to Meitei deities.

questions.q: Gotipua, a traditional dance from Odisha where young boys dress as female dancers and perform complex acrobatic postures (Bandhas) to praise Lord Jagannath, is the direct historical precursor of which classical Indian dance?
questions.explanation: Gotipua ("single boy") emerged in Odisha during the 16th century when the Devadasi (Mahari) tradition declined. Young boys trained in gymnastic flexibility and Odissi music performed acrobatic bandhas in temple courtyards, laying the foundational repertoire that revived classical Odissi in the 20th century.

questions.q: Kuchipudi takes its name from a village in which state?
questions.explanation: Kuchipudi village is in Krishna district, Andhra Pradesh.

questions.q: In which classical dance does the performer dance on the rim of a brass plate in the 'Tarangam' item?
questions.explanation: Tarangam, performed on the edges of a brass plate, is a signature Kuchipudi item.

questions.q: Which poet founded Kerala Kalamandalam in 1930 to revive Kathakali?
questions.explanation: Mahakavi Vallathol Narayana Menon founded Kerala Kalamandalam in 1930.

questions.q: Who founded Kalakshetra in 1936 and played a key role in reviving Bharatanatyam?
questions.explanation: Rukmini Devi Arundale founded Kalakshetra in Chennai in 1936.

questions.q: The 'Tribhanga' posture, with the body bent in three places, is characteristic of which classical dance?
questions.explanation: Tribhanga, along with Chowka, is a fundamental posture of Odissi.

questions.q: The 'Ras Lila' theme is central to which classical dance form?
questions.explanation: Manipuri dance is closely associated with Ras Lila depicting Radha and Krishna.

questions.q: In Kathakali make-up, the green 'Pacha' vesham is used for which type of character?
questions.explanation: Pacha (green) represents noble heroes such as Krishna and Arjuna.

questions.q: Which of the three styles of Chhau is performed without masks?
questions.explanation: Mayurbhanj Chhau of Odisha is performed without masks, unlike Purulia and Seraikela Chhau.

questions.q: Hojagiri, in which dancers balance on earthen pots and bottles, is a folk dance of which state?
questions.explanation: Hojagiri is performed by the Reang community of Tripura.

questions.q: Bagurumba, the 'butterfly dance', is a folk dance of which community?
questions.explanation: Bagurumba is a traditional dance of the Bodo community of Assam.

quizzes.title: Set 1
quizzes.subtitle: Latest GI tags: June–November 2026 and 2025-26 registrations

questions.q: Ambaji Mohanthal, the temple prasad that received a GI tag in October 2026, belongs to which state?
questions.explanation: Ambaji Mohanthal is offered as Raj Bhog at the Ambaji temple in Gujarat; the GI certificate was handed over at Ambaji in October 2026.

questions.q: Under which GI category is Ambaji Mohanthal registered?
questions.explanation: Ambaji Mohanthal is a sweet (prasad), so it is registered as a food stuff.

questions.q: Ambaji Mohanthal is mainly made from which ingredients?
options: Wheat flour, honey and dry fruits
questions.explanation: Mohanthal is a fudge of gram flour roasted in ghee and set with sugar.

questions.q: Mandar, a traditional folk drum that received a GI tag in September 2026, is from which state?
