questions.q: The GI application for the Mandar drum came from artisans of which district of Jharkhand?
questions.explanation: The applicant was an artisans’ producer company from Jarjatta village in Gumla district.

questions.q: Pithora painting, reported to have received a GI tag in August 2026, is associated with which state?
questions.explanation: Pithora is a ritual wall painting of the Rathwa and Bhilala communities of central Gujarat (Chhota Udepur).

questions.q: Pithora painting is traditionally made by which tribal community?
questions.explanation: Pithora wall paintings are made by the Rathwa (and Bhilala) communities; Warli painting belongs to Maharashtra.

questions.q: Jalbhara (Jolbhora) Sandesh, a GI-tagged sweet, comes from which town of West Bengal?
questions.explanation: Jalbhara is a sandesh with a liquid (nolen gur syrup) centre from Chandannagar.

questions.q: Chandannagar, home of the GI-tagged Jalbhara sweet, is in which district of West Bengal?
questions.explanation: Chandannagar, a former French settlement, lies in Hooghly district.

questions.q: Kuchai Silk and Bhagaiya silk, which received GI tags, belong to which state?
questions.explanation: Kuchai (Seraikela-Kharsawan) silk and Bhagaiya silk are tussar traditions of Jharkhand.

questions.q: GI-tagged Munda Jewellery is linked to the Munda tribe of which state?
questions.explanation: Munda Jewellery was among the Jharkhand products tagged in 2026, alongside Kuchai Silk and Bhagaiya silk.

questions.q: Spiti Sea Buckthorn (Chharma), which received a GI tag, is from which state?
questions.explanation: Sea buckthorn (Chharma) grows in the cold desert of Spiti in Lahaul-Spiti, Himachal Pradesh.

questions.q: In July 2026, Uttarakhand opened its first GI Products Gallery at which place?
questions.explanation: The gallery at the Uttarakhand Forest Training Academy, Haldwani, displays more than 30 GI products of the state.

questions.q: After the 2025 amendment to the GI Rules, the fee for renewing a GI registration was cut to how much?
questions.explanation: The renewal fee came down from ₹3,000 to ₹500; filing fees were cut by about 80%.

questions.q: According to the PIB backgrounder of August 2026, how many handloom products are GI-registered?
questions.explanation: The PIB note “GI Tags: Scaling Traditional Wealth into Global Brands” put GI-registered handloom products at 104.

questions.q: How many GI registrations did India have on the register as on 31 March 2026?
questions.explanation: The GI Registry’s year-wise register showed 822 registrations (including logos and foreign GIs) as on 31 March 2026.

questions.q: How many new GI tags were registered in India in FY 2025-26?
questions.explanation: 125 new GIs were registered between April 2025 and March 2026.

questions.q: Which state received the most new GI tags in FY 2025-26?
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh led with 26 new tags, followed by West Bengal with 24.

questions.q: The GI-tagged Panna Diamond belongs to which state?
questions.explanation: Panna in Madhya Pradesh has India’s only active diamond mine; Panna Diamond is one of the few “natural goods” GIs.

questions.q: Kinnauri Apple and Kinnauri Topi are GI products of which state?
questions.explanation: Kinnaur is a district of Himachal Pradesh.

questions.q: Unjha Jeera (cumin) and Unjha Fennel, registered in 2025-26, are from which state?
questions.explanation: Unjha in Mehsana district, Gujarat, is Asia’s largest spice (jeera) market.

questions.q: Patan Mashru Saree, a 2025-26 GI tag, belongs to which state?
questions.explanation: Mashru is a silk-cotton weave from Patan, Gujarat.

questions.q: Chilling Metal Work and Ladakh Thigma received GI tags for which region?
questions.explanation: Ladakh (UT) got 7 GIs in 2025-26, including Chilling Metal Work, Thigma (tie-dye) and Pabu (footwear).

questions.q: The GI-tagged Meerut Bugle is from which state?
questions.explanation: Meerut in Uttar Pradesh is known for brass musical instruments such as bugles.

questions.q: Goa Hilario and Goa Mussarad, which received GI tags, are varieties of which fruit?
questions.explanation: Hilario and Mussarad (Mankurad family) are Goan mango varieties tagged in 2025-26.

questions.q: Sirsa Kinnow, a GI-tagged citrus fruit, is from which state?
questions.explanation: Sirsa district of Haryana is a major kinnow belt.

questions.q: Ravan Hattha (a folk string instrument) and Nagori Ashwagandha are GI products of which state?
questions.explanation: Both are from Rajasthan; Ravan Hattha is a bowed folk instrument, Nagori Ashwagandha comes from Nagaur.

questions.q: Ponduru Khadi, a GI-tagged hand-spun cotton fabric, is from which state?
questions.explanation: Ponduru in Srikakulam district, Andhra Pradesh, is famous for fine hand-spun khadi.

questions.q: Kannadippaya, the GI-tagged bamboo “mirror mat”, is a craft of which state?
questions.explanation: Kannadippaya is woven by tribal communities of Kerala’s forest areas.

questions.q: Lepcha Tungbuk (a string instrument) and Lepcha Pumtong Pulit (a flute) are GI products of which state?
questions.explanation: The Lepchas are an indigenous community of Sikkim.

quizzes.title: Set 2
quizzes.subtitle: GI law, registry and state-wise products

questions.q: Which law governs Geographical Indications in India?
options: Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999
Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Act, 2001
questions.explanation: India enacted the GI Act in 1999 to meet its obligations under the WTO TRIPS Agreement.

questions.q: The GI Act of India came into force in which year?
questions.explanation: The Act came into force on 15 September 2003.

questions.q: Which was the first product in India to receive a GI tag?
questions.explanation: Darjeeling Tea was registered as India’s first GI in 2004-05.

questions.q: Where is India’s Geographical Indications Registry located?
questions.explanation: The GI Registry in Chennai has all-India jurisdiction.

questions.q: The GI Registry functions under which department?
options: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)
Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
questions.explanation: It works under the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks in DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

questions.q: For how long is a GI registration valid before it must be renewed?
questions.explanation: A GI is valid for 10 years and can be renewed indefinitely, 10 years at a time.

questions.q: GIs are protected as intellectual property under which WTO agreement?
questions.explanation: Articles 22–24 of the TRIPS Agreement deal with geographical indications.

questions.q: Which state has the highest number of GI tags overall (state-wise register, 2026)?
questions.explanation: Uttar Pradesh leads with about 79–81 GIs, followed by Tamil Nadu.

questions.q: Which state is second in total GI tags after Uttar Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Tamil Nadu has about 74–76 GIs.

questions.q: What target has the government set for GI registrations by 2030?
questions.explanation: The government aims for 10,000 GI registrations by 2030.

questions.q: Which category accounts for the largest share of India’s GI tags?
questions.explanation: Handicrafts make up about 43% (350 of 822); agricultural goods about 31%.

questions.q: Which of the following is a “natural goods” GI?
questions.explanation: Natural-goods GIs are few: Makrana Marble, Chunar Balua Patthar, Lac of Purulia, Panna Diamond and Ambaji White Marble.

questions.q: Chunar Balua Patthar, a GI from Uttar Pradesh, is a type of what?
questions.explanation: “Balua patthar” means sandstone; Chunar sandstone was used for Ashokan pillars.

questions.q: Lakadong turmeric, known for its high curcumin content, is a GI product of which state?
questions.explanation: Lakadong turmeric from the Jaintia Hills, Meghalaya, received its GI in March 2024.

questions.q: Kandhamal Haladi (turmeric) is a GI product of which state?
questions.explanation: Kandhamal turmeric from Odisha was tagged in 2019.

questions.q: Mahoba Desawari Pan (betel leaf) belongs to which state?
questions.explanation: Mahoba is in the Bundelkhand region of Uttar Pradesh.

questions.q: Kumbakonam Betel Leaf, GI-tagged in 2025, is from which state?
questions.explanation: Kumbakonam is in Thanjavur district, Tamil Nadu.

questions.q: Kolhapur Jaggery is a GI product of which state?
questions.explanation: Kolhapur in Maharashtra is famous for its jaggery (gul).

questions.q: Woraiyur Cotton Sari and Thooyamalli Rice are GI products of which state?
questions.explanation: They were among five Tamil Nadu GIs registered in December 2025 and reported in November 2026.

questions.q: Bihu Pepa, a pipe made from buffalo horn, is a GI product of which state?
questions.explanation: The pepa is played during Bohag Bihu in Assam.

questions.q: Nalanda Bawanbuti Saree is a GI product of which state?
questions.explanation: Bawanbuti (52 motifs) weaving comes from Nalanda district, Bihar.

questions.q: Badri Cow Ghee and the Bedu fruit are GI products of which state?
questions.explanation: The Badri is a hill cattle breed of Uttarakhand; Bedu is a wild Himalayan fig.

questions.q: Burhanpur Kela (banana) received a GI tag for which state?
questions.explanation: Burhanpur district of Madhya Pradesh is a major banana-growing area.

questions.q: Santiniketan Batik and Krishnanagar Clay Doll are GI products of which state?
questions.explanation: West Bengal received 24 GIs in 2025-26, second only to Madhya Pradesh.

questions.q: Mysore Silk is a GI product of which state?
questions.explanation: Mysore Silk sarees are made by KSIC in Karnataka.

questions.q: Pochampally Ikat is a GI-tagged textile of which state?
questions.explanation: Pochampally in Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district, Telangana, is known as the Silk City of India.

questions.q: Mushqbudji, an aromatic short-grain rice with a GI tag, is from which region?
questions.explanation: Mushqbudji rice is grown in Kashmir’s Anantnag district.

questions.q: Nandurbar Amchur (dried mango powder) is a GI product of which state?
questions.explanation: Nandurbar Amchur was registered in March 2024.

questions.q: Under the GI Act, a producer registered to use a GI on their goods is called what?
questions.explanation: The registered proprietor is the association or body that holds the GI; producers register as authorised users.

questions.q: The GI-tagged Tirupati Laddu belongs to which state?
questions.explanation: Tirupati Laddu, the prasad of Tirumala temple, received a GI tag in 2009.

questions.q: On which date did the Constituent Assembly adopt the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation: 26 November is observed as Constitution Day; the Constitution came into effect on 26 January 1950.

questions.q: How long did the Constituent Assembly take to frame the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Work ran from 9 December 1946 to 26 November 1949.

questions.q: Who did the English calligraphy of the original Constitution?
questions.explanation: Vasant Krishan Vaidya did the Hindi calligraphy; Nandalal Bose and his students decorated the pages.

questions.q: The pages of the original Constitution were decorated by which artist and his students?
questions.explanation: Nandalal Bose and students of Kala Bhavan, Santiniketan, illuminated the pages.

questions.q: How many Articles, Parts and Schedules did the original Constitution have?
questions.explanation: It has since grown to over 470 Articles, 25 Parts and 12 Schedules.

questions.q: The Preamble has been amended only once, by which Amendment?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment, called the “Mini-Constitution”, amended the Preamble.

questions.q: Which words were added to the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment inserted “Socialist”, “Secular” and “Integrity”.

questions.q: Which Schedule contains the Union List, State List and Concurrent List?
questions.explanation: The Seventh Schedule divides legislative subjects between the Union and the States.

questions.q: The Anti-Defection Law is contained in which Schedule?
questions.explanation: The Tenth Schedule was added by the 52nd Amendment in 1985.

questions.q: How many subjects are listed for Panchayats in the Eleventh Schedule?
questions.explanation: The Eleventh Schedule lists 29 subjects for Panchayats; the Twelfth lists 18 for Municipalities.

questions.q: Fundamental Rights are contained in which Part and Articles of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Part III guarantees six Fundamental Rights.

questions.q: The Right to Property was removed from Fundamental Rights by which Amendment?
questions.explanation: It is now a legal right under Article 300A.

questions.q: The Right to Education (Article 21A) was added by which Amendment?
questions.explanation: It covers children aged 6 to 14 years.

questions.q: The Directive Principles of State Policy were borrowed from the constitution of which country?
questions.explanation: DPSPs (Part IV, Articles 36–51) are not enforceable by courts.

questions.q: Fundamental Duties were added on the recommendation of which committee?
questions.explanation: They were added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976, as Article 51A.

questions.q: Fundamental Duties are listed under which Article?
questions.explanation: Article 51A in Part IVA; the 11th duty was added in 2002.

questions.q: What is the minimum age to be elected President of India?
questions.explanation: A candidate must also be qualified for election to the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: Who is the only President of India to have served two full terms?
options: Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
questions.explanation: Rajendra Prasad served from 1950 to 1962.

questions.q: Who was the first woman President of India?
questions.explanation: Pratibha Patil was the 12th President (2007–2012).

questions.q: Who was the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: Ganesh Vasudev Mavalankar served from 1952 to 1956.

questions.q: Who was the first woman Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: Meira Kumar served from 2009 to 2014.

questions.q: What is the minimum age to become a member of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation: It is 25 years for the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the quorum of the Houses of Parliament?
questions.explanation: Quorum is one-tenth of the total membership of the House.

questions.q: Which of these states does NOT have a Legislative Council?
questions.explanation: Six states have councils: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra and Karnataka.

questions.q: What is the retirement age of a High Court judge?
questions.explanation: Supreme Court judges retire at 65.

questions.q: Who was the first Chief Justice of India?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court was inaugurated on 28 January 1950.

questions.q: Who was the first woman judge of the Supreme Court of India?
questions.explanation: Justice Fathima Beevi was appointed in 1989.

questions.q: Goa falls under the jurisdiction of which High Court?
questions.explanation: The Bombay HC covers Maharashtra, Goa, and Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu.

questions.q: The 106th Amendment Act, 2023 (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam) provides for what?
options: 33% reservation for women in Lok Sabha and State Assemblies
questions.explanation: GST came with the 101st Amendment; EWS quota with the 103rd.

questions.q: Which Amendment introduced 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS)?
questions.explanation: The 103rd Amendment applies to education and government jobs.

questions.q: Where is the headquarters of the Asian Development Bank (ADB)?
questions.explanation: ADB began operations on 19 December 1966; its President is Masato Kanda.

questions.q: The New Development Bank (formerly BRICS Development Bank) is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: It was agreed at the 6th BRICS Summit in Fortaleza (2014) and opened in 2015.

questions.q: Where is the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) headquartered?
questions.explanation: AIIB started operations in January 2016; India is its second-largest shareholder.

questions.q: Where is the ASEAN Secretariat located?
questions.explanation: ASEAN was founded on 8 August 1967 in Bangkok.

questions.q: Which country joined ASEAN as its 11th member?
questions.explanation: ASEAN now has 11 members.

questions.q: The Commonwealth Secretariat is located at which building?
questions.explanation: The Commonwealth has 56 member states.

questions.q: Where is the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) headquartered?
questions.explanation: FAO was founded on 16 October 1945 (World Food Day) in Quebec City.

questions.q: The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: The GCC charter was signed in Abu Dhabi in 1981.

questions.q: Where is the headquarters of OPEC?
questions.explanation: OPEC was founded at the Baghdad Conference in 1960 and moved to Vienna in 1965.

questions.q: What is the motto of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)?
questions.explanation: The IAEA, set up in 1957, is headquartered in Vienna.

questions.q: How many judges sit on the International Court of Justice?
questions.explanation: ICJ judges serve nine-year terms; the court sits at the Peace Palace in The Hague.

questions.q: Where is the headquarters of INTERPOL?
Where is the secretariat of the International Solar Alliance (ISA)?
questions.explanation: It is on the National Institute of Solar Energy (NISE) campus in Gurugram.

questions.q: India launched the International Solar Alliance in 2015 together with which country?
questions.explanation: It was launched on 30 November 2015 at COP21 in Paris.

questions.q: The World Economic Forum is headquartered at which place?
questions.explanation: Its annual meeting is held in Davos, but the headquarters is in Cologny near Geneva.

questions.q: Who is the Director General of WIPO?
questions.explanation: WIPO, headquartered in Geneva, became a UN specialised agency in 1974.

questions.q: Who is the President of the World Bank Group?
questions.explanation: Ajay Banga, the 14th President, took office on 2 June 2023.

questions.q: Who is the Director-General of the World Trade Organization?
questions.explanation: The WTO, headquartered in Geneva, was set up on 1 January 1995.

questions.q: Where is the headquarters of WWF (World Wide Fund for Nature)?
questions.explanation: WWF was formed on 29 April 1961.

questions.q: On which date was ISRO established?
questions.explanation: ISRO is headquartered in Bengaluru; its motto is “Space technology in the service of humankind”.

questions.q: Who is the CEO and MD of LIC?
questions.explanation: He took charge on 14 July 2025; LIC is headquartered in Mumbai.

questions.q: Where is the headquarters of SIDBI?
questions.explanation: SIDBI was set up on 2 April 1990.

questions.q: IRDAI is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: IRDAI moved from Delhi to Hyderabad in 2001; its chairperson is Ajay Seth.

questions.q: Who is the Chairman of SEBI?
questions.explanation: He took office on 1 March 2025.

questions.q: Which country hosted the 18th BRICS Summit in September 2026?
questions.explanation: It was held in New Delhi and adopted the New Delhi Declaration; China hosts in 2027.

questions.q: Which country holds the G20 presidency in 2026?
questions.explanation: South Africa hosted in 2025; the UK will host in 2027.

questions.q: The Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS) of the SCO is located in which city?
questions.explanation: The SCO Secretariat is in Beijing.

questions.q: Where is the permanent headquarters of the UNFCCC?
questions.explanation: The UNFCCC was set up at the 1992 Rio Earth Summit.

questions.q: Which city hosted CBD COP17 (Convention on Biological Diversity) in October 2026?
questions.explanation: The CBD secretariat is in Montreal.

questions.q: Where was the 2026 NATO Summit held?
questions.explanation: It was held on 7–8 July 2026; Türkiye earlier hosted in Istanbul in 2004.

quizzes.title: Set 3
quizzes.subtitle: Space missions, rivers, lakes, cities and national parks

questions.q: Which was India’s first indigenously built satellite?
questions.explanation: Aryabhata was launched in 1975.

questions.q: Chandrayaan-1 (2008) made which landmark discovery?
options: A new lunar crater named Shiv Shakti
Water molecules on the Moon’s surface
questions.explanation: It was India’s first lunar probe.

questions.q: The Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan) made India the first Asian nation to reach Mars orbit. In which year was it launched?
questions.explanation: India was also the first country to succeed on its maiden attempt.

questions.q: Chandrayaan-3 (2023) achieved the world’s first soft landing near which part of the Moon?
questions.explanation: India became the fourth country to land on the Moon.

questions.q: Aditya-L1, India’s solar observatory, is placed in a halo orbit around which point?
questions.explanation: L1 lies between the Earth and the Sun.

questions.q: XPoSat (2024) is India’s first dedicated mission for what?
questions.explanation: It studies bright X-ray sources such as black holes and neutron stars.

questions.q: The SpaDeX mission demonstrated which capability?
questions.explanation: India became the fourth nation with orbital docking capability.

questions.q: Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla went to the International Space Station in 2025 on which mission?
questions.explanation: He was later awarded the Ashoka Chakra.

questions.q: NISAR is a joint Earth-observation mission between ISRO and which agency?
questions.explanation: It is the first joint hardware mission of ISRO and NASA.

questions.q: Which humanoid robot flies on the uncrewed Gaganyaan test flights?
questions.explanation: The flights validate human-rating systems before crewed missions.

questions.q: Shukrayaan-1 is ISRO’s planned mission to which planet?
questions.explanation: It is planned for 2028.

questions.q: Chandrayaan-5 / LUPEX is a joint lunar polar mission of ISRO and which agency?
questions.explanation: India provides the lander and Japan the rover.

questions.q: Which is the longest river flowing within India?
questions.explanation: The Ganga is about 2,525 km long and rises from the Gangotri Glacier.

questions.q: Which is India’s largest river by water volume?
questions.explanation: Its channel is up to 8–10 km wide.

questions.q: Which river is called the “Dakshin Ganga”?
questions.explanation: At about 1,465 km, it is the longest river of peninsular India.

questions.q: Which is the longest tributary of the Ganga?
questions.explanation: The Yamuna is about 1,376 km long.

questions.q: Which is the longest west-flowing river of India?
questions.explanation: The Narmada flows through a rift valley into the Gulf of Khambhat.

questions.q: Which is the largest freshwater lake in India?
questions.explanation: Wular (J&K) was formed by tectonic activity; Chilika is a brackish lagoon.

questions.q: Which is the longest lake in India?
questions.explanation: Vembanad stretches across Kerala’s backwaters.

questions.q: Lonar Lake in Maharashtra was formed by what?
questions.explanation: It is a saline, soda crater lake.

questions.q: Which is the highest waterfall in India?
questions.explanation: At 455 m, Kunchikal near Agumbe, Karnataka, is formed by the Varahi river.

questions.q: Chitrakote Falls, the “Niagara of India”, is on which river?
questions.explanation: It is in Chhattisgarh and is India’s widest waterfall.

questions.q: Which city is known as the “Manchester of India”?
questions.explanation: Ahmedabad is also called the Heritage City.

questions.q: Which city is called the “Queen of the Arabian Sea”?
questions.explanation: Alappuzha is called the “Venice of the East”.

questions.q: Which is the largest national park in India?
questions.explanation: Hemis in Ladakh is also the highest-altitude park, known for snow leopards.

questions.q: Keibul Lamjao, the world’s only floating national park, is the natural habitat of which animal?
questions.explanation: It sits on phumdis in Loktak Lake, Manipur.

questions.q: Which state has the most national parks in India?
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh has 11 national parks and is called the “Tiger State”.

questions.q: Which is the only state in India with no notified national park?
questions.explanation: Punjab has 13 wildlife sanctuaries but no national park.

questions.q: Which is the largest tiger reserve in India?
questions.explanation: It spans about 3,296 sq km in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

questions.q: Similipal in Odisha is the only natural habitat of which animal?
questions.explanation: Similipal is in Mayurbhanj district.

quizzes.title: Set 4
quizzes.subtitle: Awards, heritage, Ramsar, codes, books and arts

questions.q: Where is the Nobel Peace Prize presented?
questions.explanation: All other Nobel prizes are presented in Stockholm on 10 December.

questions.q: Who is the youngest person to receive a Nobel Prize?
questions.explanation: She won the Peace Prize at 17, in 2014.

questions.q: C. V. Raman received the Nobel Prize in Physics in which year?
questions.explanation: It was for the Raman Effect, the scattering of light.

questions.q: Who was the first Indian to receive the Ramon Magsaysay Award?
questions.explanation: He won the first award in 1958 for leading the Bhoodan movement.

questions.q: Which became the first Indian organisation to win the Ramon Magsaysay Award (2025)?
questions.explanation: The Foundation to Educate Girls Globally was honoured for girls’ education in rural India.

questions.q: Who won the Booker Prize 2026?
questions.explanation: He won for “The End of Everything” and, at 81, became the oldest winner.

questions.q: Arundhati Roy won the Booker Prize in 1997 for which novel?
questions.explanation: Kiran Desai, Aravind Adiga and Salman Rushdie wrote the others.

questions.q: The Pulitzer Prize is administered by which university?
questions.explanation: The first Pulitzer Prizes were awarded in 1917.

questions.q: Who was the first recipient of the World Food Prize (1987)?
questions.explanation: The prize was founded by Norman Borlaug in 1986.

questions.q: Who was the first recipient of the Jnanpith Award (1965)?
questions.explanation: The Malayalam poet won for “Odakkuzhal” (The Bamboo Flute).

questions.q: Who was the first woman to receive the Jnanpith Award?
questions.explanation: The Bengali novelist won in 1976 for “Prothom Protishruti”.

questions.q: In how many languages is the Sahitya Akademi Award given?
questions.explanation: The 22 Eighth Schedule languages, plus English and Rajasthani.

questions.q: Who was the first recipient of the Khel Ratna Award (1991–92)?
questions.explanation: It is now called the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award.

questions.q: The Dronacharya Award is presented on National Sports Day. When is National Sports Day?
questions.explanation: 29 August is Major Dhyan Chand’s birth anniversary.

questions.q: Who was the first recipient of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award?
questions.explanation: She received it at the 17th National Film Awards in 1969.

questions.q: Who was the first Indian to win an Oscar?
questions.explanation: She won Best Costume Design for “Gandhi” in 1983.

questions.q: What is the normal limit on the number of Padma awards given in a year?
questions.explanation: The limit excludes posthumous awards and awards to NRIs, foreigners and OCIs.

questions.q: Which is the highest peacetime gallantry award in India?
questions.explanation: Param Vir Chakra is the highest wartime gallantry award.

questions.q: The Kirti Chakra was earlier known by which name?
questions.explanation: The classes were renamed in January 1967.

questions.q: Which is India’s only “mixed” UNESCO World Heritage Site?
questions.explanation: It is valued for both natural and cultural significance.

questions.q: Which of these is on UNESCO’s Intangible Cultural Heritage list for India?
questions.explanation: India’s 16 elements include Kumbh Mela, Durga Puja, Garba and Deepavali.

questions.q: Where was the Ramsar Convention on wetlands adopted?
questions.explanation: It was adopted on 2 February 1971 (World Wetlands Day).

questions.q: Which were India’s first Ramsar sites (1981)?
options: Chilika Lake and Keoladeo National Park
Sambhar Lake and Keoladeo National Park
questions.explanation: Both were designated on 1 October 1981.

questions.q: Which state has the highest number of Ramsar sites in India?
questions.explanation: Tamil Nadu has 20 sites.

questions.q: Which two Indian sites are on the Montreux Record?
options: Keoladeo National Park and Loktak Lake
questions.explanation: Chilika was removed from the Montreux Record in 2002 after restoration.

questions.q: In a PAN, what does the 4th character “P” stand for?
questions.explanation: C = Company, H = HUF, F = Firm/LLP, T = Trust, G = Government.

questions.q: The Universal Account Number (UAN) issued by EPFO has how many digits?
questions.explanation: One UAN links all PF member IDs across employers.

questions.q: “Gita Rahasya” was written by whom?
questions.explanation: Tilak also ran the papers “Kesari” and “The Maratha”.

questions.q: Sattriya, one of India’s classical dances, belongs to which state?
questions.explanation: Kerala has Kathakali and Mohiniyattam; Manipur has Manipuri.

questions.q: Ustad Zakir Hussain is associated with which instrument?
questions.explanation: Ravi Shankar played sitar, Shivkumar Sharma santoor and Bismillah Khan shehnai.
